microtheory.name: gastronomy
microtheory.definition: Gastronomy — the art + science of food + cuisine. Culinary techniques, flavor + taste science, food chemistry + physics, cuisine traditions, food culture, molecular gastronomy. Brillat-Savarin, Carême, Escoffier, Point, Bocuse, Adrià, Achatz, McGee. Substrate analogue: applied chemistry + craft + culture transforming raw inputs into transmissive cultural objects.

concepts.name: gastronomy_definition
concepts.definition: Brillat-Savarin 1825. 'Reasoned knowledge of everything connected with man's nourishment.' Beyond just cooking — physiology, chemistry, sociology, aesthetics.

concepts.name: cuisine
concepts.definition: Style of cooking characteristic of place or tradition. French, Chinese, Italian, Japanese, Indian, Mexican, Persian. Substrate analogue: substrate's place-bound transmissive style.

concepts.name: brillat_savarin
concepts.definition: Jean Anthelme Brillat-Savarin 1825 'The Physiology of Taste'. Aphorisms: 'Tell me what you eat...'. Founded gastronomy as discipline.

concepts.name: terroir
concepts.definition: French. Place's effect on taste of produce. Geology + climate + tradition. Wine + cheese + coffee paradigmatic.

concepts.name: taste_sense
concepts.definition: Five basic: sweet, sour, salty, bitter, umami (Ikeda 1908). Possible additions: fat, calcium, kokumi. Substrate analogue: substrate's primitive chemical sensors.

concepts.name: umami
concepts.definition: Glutamate detection. Discovered by Ikeda 1908 in kombu broth. Foundation of broth + parmesan + tomato + mushroom appeal.

concepts.name: flavor
concepts.definition: Taste + smell + texture + temperature + appearance integrated. 80% is olfaction. Retronasal olfaction key.

concepts.name: retronasal_olfaction
concepts.definition: Smell through back of mouth as food chewed. Distinct from orthonasal (sniffing). Where most 'flavor' is.

concepts.name: mouthfeel
concepts.definition: Texture + temperature + pungency + astringency + carbonation. Major flavor component. Texture as important as taste.

concepts.name: maillard_reaction
concepts.definition: Louis-Camille Maillard 1912. Amino acid + reducing sugar at heat → hundreds of flavor compounds. Browning of bread + meat + coffee + chocolate.

concepts.name: caramelisation
concepts.definition: Sugar pyrolysis at high heat. Distinct from Maillard. ~160°C+. Nutty, buttery, complex.

concepts.name: emulsion
concepts.definition: Suspension of oil + water with emulsifier. Mayo, hollandaise, vinaigrette. Lecithin in egg yolk classic.

concepts.name: denaturation_protein
concepts.definition: Heat + acid + agitation unfolds protein structure. Cooking eggs, curing fish, whipping cream.

concepts.name: starch_gelatinisation
concepts.definition: Starch + water + heat → swollen amylose + amylopectin. Rice cooking, sauce thickening, bread interior.

concepts.name: fermentation_food
concepts.definition: Microbial transformation. Bread, beer, wine, cheese, yogurt, kimchi, sauerkraut, miso. Preservation + flavor.

concepts.name: cooking_techniques
concepts.definition: Boiling, steaming, poaching, sautéing, frying, roasting, grilling, braising, sous vide, baking, smoking, fermenting, curing.

concepts.name: sous_vide
concepts.definition: Vacuum-sealed cooking in precise temperature water bath. Long times, exact doneness. Pioneered 1970s; modern home availability ~2010s.

concepts.name: braising
concepts.definition: Sear + low slow moist cooking. Tough cuts → tender. Collagen → gelatin. Stews, coq au vin, brisket.

concepts.name: stock_making
concepts.definition: Long simmer of bones + aromatics + water. Extracts gelatin + glutamates. Foundation of classical French.

concepts.name: knife_skills
concepts.definition: Foundational technique. Brunoise, julienne, chiffonade, dice. Consistent size = consistent cooking.

concepts.name: auguste_escoffier
concepts.definition: Auguste Escoffier 1903 'Le Guide Culinaire'. Codified French cuisine + brigade kitchen system. Bridge from classical to modern.

concepts.name: marie_antoine_careme
concepts.definition: Carême ~1820s. Founder of grande cuisine. Architectural pièces montées. Mother sauces taxonomy.

concepts.name: nouvelle_cuisine
concepts.definition: 1960s-70s France. Bocuse, Troisgros, Guérard, Vergé. Lighter, fresher, shorter cooking, presentation. Rebellion against classical heaviness.

concepts.name: molecular_gastronomy
concepts.definition: Hervé This + Nicholas Kurti coined 1992. Apply chemistry + physics to cooking. Adrià, Achatz, Blumenthal influential.

concepts.name: ferran_adria
concepts.definition: El Bulli (closed 2011). Spherification, foams, deconstruction. Most influential chef of late 20th c.

concepts.name: harold_mcgee
concepts.definition: On Food and Cooking 1984. Made food science accessible to cooks. Reference work.

concepts.name: mother_sauces
concepts.definition: Carême + Escoffier. Béchamel + velouté + espagnole + tomato + hollandaise. Foundations from which others derive.

concepts.name: mise_en_place
concepts.definition: 'Putting in place'. All ingredients prepped + arranged before cooking begins. Foundation of professional kitchen discipline.

concepts.name: brigade_kitchen
concepts.definition: Escoffier. Hierarchical station system. Chef de cuisine + sous chef + chef de partie + commis. Efficient parallel production.

concepts.name: cuisine_traditions
concepts.definition: Each developed under constraints: ingredients available, fuel, religion, history. Convergent solutions to similar problems across cultures.

concepts.name: french_cuisine
concepts.definition: Codified through monarchy + republic. Mother sauces, technique-centric, butter + wine + cream. UNESCO heritage 2010.

concepts.name: italian_cuisine
concepts.definition: Regional more than national. Ingredient-driven. Pasta + olive oil + tomato + cheese + bread. Simple combinations.

concepts.name: japanese_cuisine
concepts.definition: Seasonality + presentation + dashi as umami base. Sushi + ramen + tempura + kaiseki. Minimal intervention philosophy.

concepts.name: chinese_cuisine
concepts.definition: Regional traditions (Sichuan, Cantonese, Hunan, Shandong, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Anhui). Heat-control + wok + balance.

concepts.name: indian_cuisine
concepts.definition: Spice complexity. Regional variation enormous. Vegetarian + meat. Religion + caste shape.

concepts.name: food_pairing_theory
concepts.definition: Foods sharing key flavor compounds may pair well. Foodpairing.com. Chocolate + blue cheese share methylpyrazines.

concepts.name: kokumi
concepts.definition: Sensation of richness + thickness + persistence. Distinct from umami. Glutathione + γ-glutamyl peptides involved.

concepts.name: fermentation_revival
concepts.definition: Sandor Katz + Noma. Wild fermentation + lab-cultured + traditional revival. Restaurant-driven movement post-2010.

rules.name: flavor_is_multimodal_integration
rules.head: Jabberwock evaluates a food experience
rules.body: flavor = taste + smell (mostly retronasal) + texture + temperature + appearance integrated. 80% is olfaction. Substrate's multisensory binding.

rules.name: maillard_reaction_produces_savory_complexity
rules.head: Jabberwock cooks protein-containing food at high heat
rules.body: Maillard reaction (amino acid + reducing sugar) produces hundreds of flavor compounds. Browning of crust. Distinct from caramelisation (sugar alone).

rules.name: mise_en_place_enables_complex_execution
rules.head: Jabberwock prepares to cook complex dish
rules.body: all ingredients prepped + measured + arranged before cooking starts. Allows focused attention on technique + timing. Substrate's planning-before-execution discipline.

rules.name: technique_compounds_with_ingredient_quality
rules.head: Jabberwock evaluates dish potential
rules.body: great technique on poor ingredients yields mediocre result; great ingredients with poor technique yields mediocre result. Both required.

rules.name: fermentation_extends_storage_and_complexity
rules.head: Jabberwock examines traditional food preservation
rules.body: microbial fermentation extends storage life + develops complex flavor + nutritional changes. Universal across cultures (bread, wine, cheese, kimchi, miso).
